Sorption data fit well with the Freundlich model, with logKF values increasing from 0.476 (MS350) to 0.771 (MS550), reaching 1.865 for MS750, highlighting stronger sorb affinity and capacity at higher pyrolysis temperatures. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed that atrazine sorption onto BC-amended soil is spontaneous, endothermic, and primarily governed by physisorption mechanisms. Additionally, lower soil pH enhanced the sorption of atrazine in BC-treated soils.\n\nOverall, the findings demonstrate that BC acts as an efficient sorbent for atrazine removal in tropical soils, with sorption capacity and kinetics improving with higher pyrolysis temperatures. The presence of owl material can harbor ectoparasites such as fleas that may overwinter and infest new occupants. To understand how owl material influences nest reuse, researchers manipulated artificial burrows previously used by owls by applying three treatments: (1) complete removal of owl material from entrance, tunnel, and nesting chamber, replaced with fresh soil; (2) microwaving owl material to kill ectoparasites before returning it; and (3) removing and then returning owl material without treatment as a control. Results showed that burrows retaining owl material, both in control and microwaved treatments, were reused by burrowing owls 3.5 to 3.8 times more than burrows where owl material was removed. Microwaving did not improve reuse over control burrows, and flea infestations were found in all treatment groups, indicating that removing ectoparasites via owl material treatment did not enhance nest-site selection. The presence of owl material may serve as a cue for owls locating specific burrows upon return from migration or may offer physiological or feeding benefits. Consequently, removal of owl material from artificial burrows may reduce the likelihood of reuse, suggesting that nest cleaning aimed at increasing burrowing owl occupancy could be counterproductive. Maintaining owl material in artificial burrows appears beneficial for maximizing reuse and effective burrowing owl management.",

This allows dynamic adjustment of large spatial receptive fields, improving the identification of disease features from UAV perspectives. Additionally, the neck of the network incorporates the GSConv hybrid convolution module, reducing computational load and parameters while maintaining performance. Recognizing that disease symptoms on wild rice kernels can appear elongated and rotated when viewed aerially, the model\u2019s head layer outputs an added rotational angle (theta dimension), enabling precise detection of bacterial blight regardless of orientation.\n\nExperimental results demonstrate the Xoo-YOLO model\u2019s superior performance, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 94.95%, surpassing other competing models. This balance between accuracy and speed establishes the Xoo-YOLO model as a key technological advance for the intelligent, large-scale identification of disease resistance in wild rice kernels. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_02021343": "batter-or breadcrumb-coated products are highly attractive foods. coatings enhance the flavor, texture, and appearance, adding value to the substrate food by giving the fried product a pleasant golden color and a crispy exterior texture that is normally very appetizing. because \"battering and frying\" has been a traditional method for preparing foods, empiricism has dominated its application for decades. although considerable geographical variations occasionally exist because of the raw materials available, versions of batter-coated or breaded foods are found in the traditional or regional cuisines of practically every part of the world. changes in lifestyle, particularly in the western world, have consolidated the availability and sales of convenience foods and frozen products, providing considerable support for the expansion and globalization of coated foods. nowadays, the market for this type of product is growing steadily, and there are even major food service sector companies with a worldwide presence that only serve products of this kind. automation of manufacturing, innovations in the cooking methods, the demand for more sophisticated foods, diversification, and a concern to develop healthier products that contain less fat are the factors that dominate the latest research trends in this area. in addition, if the products are to go through the final cooking stage in the home there has to be a certain degree of versatility, as the consumer can vary the method or times and this should not lead to disappointment. the research fields have been increasing permanently in recent years. they cover developments in both coating formulations and coating application technology, which constitute the important challenges facing the technicians and researchers working in this area. in the traditional process, the manufacturer batters the food pieces (chicken pieces, chicken nuggets, and strips, beef fritters and fingers, pork chunks, veal products, etc.), prefries them for a few seconds in order to give the batter a certain solidity of consistence, and then freezes them. the consumer buys them in this form and, in turn, fries them for a few minutes in order to cook them, normally until a golden external color has been reached. from the point of view of the industrial process, there is a choice between cooking fully before the application of the coating (95\u00b0c, 99% rh) or after it (180\u00b0c, 5% rh); in both cases the coating stage is followed by a prefrying step. the choice depends on the industrial machinery, the type of meat or other product to be coated, and its size, shape, etc., but it must also be remembered that yields can differ considerably, as can the final product quality. while the batter is raw it must create a homogeneous layer that covers the food, which is normally also raw, and must adhere to it before and after coagulation - which takes place during the prefrying step - and during final frying; after the batter coagulates it must withstand freezing temperatures and normal handling (packaging and transportation) without cracking or breaking and without losing any portion of the external layer; during the final frying performed in the consumer's home it must create an outer crust with good acceptability in terms of texture (particularly crispness), flavor, and color. coatings might also need to prevent oxidation, limit moisture and oil transfer, give freeze/thaw stability, and extend shelf life. of course, they must also be cost-effective (kuntz, 1997a). to achieve these objectives, research into the behavior of flours and starches has traveled a long way and a considerable array of ingredients with a broad range of functionalities has begun to be used. methods for controlling the physical properties of both the raw and the fried products have also seen a tremendous boost in recent decades. although the fascinating world of battered or breaded foods involves many technological aspects, this chapter will pay particular attention to the use of ingredients and their properties in relation to good coated product performance and, more specifically, to the uses of polysaccharide hydrocolloids or gums, which have such a wide-ranging functionality that they feature in practically every approach to improving the quality of coated products. most of the available information for studying the ingredients used in these types of coatings does not differ greatly between meat products and other types of foods although, in fact, most of the developments have been made for protein substrates. nevertheless, developments involving specific aspects of meat products will be cited in detail in this chapter. \u00a9 2009 springer science "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03414425": "The text discusses the use of chemical additives, particularly sulfate-containing additives such as sodium sulphates, in concrete technology to address various problems and to serve as accelerators for the setting and hardening of cement. The mechanism by which these additive accelerators, including sodium sulphates, influence cement hydration is complex and not fully established. Sodium sulphates accelerate the hydration of cement's silicate phases primarily by increasing the ionic strength of the solution. Additionally, sodium sulphates participate in exchange reactions with portlandite (Ca(OH)2) and aluminate phases in the cement, resulting in the formation of soluble hydroxides and poorly soluble calcium salts, which significantly affect the hardening process.\n\nThe effects of sulfate-containing additives, such as sodium sulphates, on the properties of water-cement paste and hardened cement vary widely and depend on factors such as salt concentration and the type of cation present. For instance, aluminum sulphate additives behave differently due to hydrolysis in alkaline conditions, which further accelerates cement setting. Despite the similarity among these additives in providing anions for exchange reactions, the mechanisms by which sodium sulphates and aluminum sulphate influence cement setting and hardening differ substantially.\n\nThe paper focuses on the thermochemical aspects of these interactions, particularly the behavior of sodium sulphates and aluminum sulphate additives in cement compositions. It presents thermochemical equations describing the reactions between sulfate-containing additives like sodium sulphates and the hydrated phases of cement clinker. Moreover, the paper outlines methods for calculating the thermal effects of these chemical reactions and assessing how the resulting products impact the setting and hardening processes of Portland cement. This thermochemical perspective provides valuable insights into the role of sodium sulphates in modifying cement hydration and hardening behavior.",

KBV transmits both vertically, from queen to larvae, and horizontally, often through contaminated food sources. Importantly, plants pollinated by bees, including the mountain papaya plant (Vasconcellea pubescens), can serve as reservoirs for horizontal transmission of KBV. This occurs when infected pollinators contaminate pollen and flowers with feces, facilitating virus spread both within and between species.\n\nIn this study, KBV sequences were investigated specifically within the transcriptomes of the mountain papaya plant. Transcriptomic data from fruit, leaves, and root tissues of the mountain papaya plant were mapped to the KBV reference genome, achieving 91% coverage. Phylogenetic analysis demonstrated that the KBV-Ch sequence shares 97% nucleotide identity with the KBV reference genome and clusters with other KBV strains previously isolated from Spain, Chile, and New Zealand.\n\nThese findings confirm the presence of KBV genetic material in the mountain papaya plant, highlighting its role not just as an economically important species but also as a potential environmental reservoir facilitating KBV horizontal transmission. The study underscores the importance of the mountain papaya plant in the ecology of KBV spread, reinforcing concerns about pollinator-mediated virus transmission routes through pollinated plants. Thus, the mountain papaya plant is implicated as a key player in both sustaining and potentially disseminating KBV among pollinator communities, with possible broader impacts on honeybee health and pollination dynamics.",

A model describing the behavior of Zn fertilizers in the soil-plant system was developed, highlighting that synthetic chelates like ZnEDTA operate via a shuttle effect to mobilize Zn, while Zn-LS complexes deliver Zn directly within the rhizosphere. Overall, while ZnEDTA remains superior in facilitating both fertilizer and native Zn uptake by navy bean plants, ZnLSE represents a promising eco-friendly alternative, especially when applied at higher doses. presumably allopolyploid species occurring in the south island of new zealand and in tasmania. all pachycladon species possess ten chromosome pairs (2n = 20). the feasibility of comparative chromosome painting (ccp) in crucifer species allows the origin and genome evolution in this genus to be elucidated. we focus on the origin and genome evolution of pachycladon as well as on its genomic relationship to other crucifer species, particularly to the allopolyploid australian camelineae taxa. as species radiation on islands is usually characterized by chromosomal stasis, i.e. uniformity of chromosome numbers/ploidy levels, the role of major karyotypic reshuffling during the island adaptive and species radiation in pachycladon is investigated through whole-genome ccp analysis. results. the four analyzed pachycladon species possess an identical karyotype structure. the consensual ancestral karyotype is most likely common to all pachycladon species and corroborates the monophyletic origin of the genus evidenced by previous phylogenetic analyses. the ancestral pachycladon karyotype (n = 10) originated through an allopolyploidization event between two genomes structurally resembling the ancestral crucifer karyotype (ack, n = 8). the primary allopolyploid (apparently with n = 16) has undergone genome reshuffling by descending dysploidy toward n = 10. chromosome \"fusions\" were mediated by inversions, translocations and centromere inactivation/loss. pachycladon chromosome 3 (pc3) resulted from insertional fusion, described in grasses. the allopolyploid ancestor originated in australia, from the same or closely related ack-like parental species as the australian camelineae allopolyploids. however, the two whole-genome duplication (wgd) events were independent, with the pachycladon wgd being significantly younger. the long-distance dispersal of the diploidized pachycladon ancestor to new zealand was followed by the pleistocene species radiation in alpine habitats and characterized by karyotypic stasis. conclusions. karyotypic stasis in pachycladon suggests that the insular species radiation in this genus proceeded through homoploid divergence rather than through species-specific gross chromosomal repatterning. the ancestral pachycladon genome originated in australia through an allopolyploidization event involving two closely related parental genomes, and spread to new zealand by a long-distance dispersal. we argue that the chromosome number decrease mediated by inter-genomic reshuffling (diploidization) could provide the pachycladon allopolyploid founder with an adaptive advantage to colonize montane/alpine habitats. the ancestral pachycladon karyotype remained stable during the pleistocene adaptive radiation into ten This blandness can be improved by blending raw chayote with suitable substrates like sugarcane juice combined with natural flavorings. However, preserving spiced juice made from raw chayote and sugarcane juice presents challenges since both juices are susceptible to microbial spoilage. The study aimed to preserve spiced chayote juice through hurdle technology by applying different pasteurization conditions\u2014temperatures of 70 \u00b0C and 80 \u00b0C for 10 and 20 minutes\u2014followed by adding varying concentrations of potassium metabisulphite (KMS) at 200, 300, and 400 ppm. Sunflower seeds and lipid-containing fluid were recovered from the euthanized alpaca\u2019s digestive system. Overall, three of the four alpacas either died or were euthanized, with only one surviving following outpatient therapy.\n\nThis case series highlights the significant morbidity and high mortality linked to ingestion of lipid-rich black oil sunflower seeds in alpacas. The large lipid load from sunflower seed oil likely inhibited forestomach bacterial activity and coated fibrous feed, overwhelming the alpacas\u2019 ability to metabolize unsaturated lipids. Additionally, the physical hulls of the sunflower seeds appeared to cause traumatic damage to the esophageal and forestomach mucosa, resulting in ulcerations and potential sepsis.\n\nIn conclusion, excessive lipid intake from sources such as black oil sunflower seeds, which are high in sunflower seed oil, can be fatal to alpacas. Diets high in lipid content including black oil sunflower seeds should be avoided in camelids to prevent such toxicities. This report underscores the risks associated with feeding sunflower seed oil-containing products to alpacas and the need for caution regarding lipid-rich feedstuffs in their diet.",

Additionally, this study demonstrated the effectiveness of ultrasound imaging as a non-invasive tool for assessing meat quality traits in Wagyu cattle, Bali cattle, and their cross-breeds. other means. moreover, due to many reasons, there is a lack of varieties with good comprehensive characteristics. finally, it is difficult to study genes in banana through the forward or reverse genetic means, limiting the molecular research on banana. in the future, we should: (1) continue to strengthen the collection, evaluation and utilization of global banana germplasm resources, and Researchers examined utricular afferent responses in toadfish under normal gravity (1 g) conditions to establish baseline data and after exposure to hypergravity (HG) conditions created by centrifugation at 2.24 g for durations ranging from 1 to 32 days. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03490151": "The scalability and flexibility of modern cloud applications largely rely on virtual machines (VMs) and containers. VMs are isolated operating systems running on a hypervisor, while containers are lightweight isolated processes sharing the host OS kernel. In typical bare-metal servers, multiple VMs coexist, each running multiple containers and containerized applications that share common images (libraries and code). However, container image sharing is optimized primarily within a single VM and is nearly nonexistent across multiple VMs, even when these VMs reside on the same bare-metal server. This VM isolation results in repetitive image downloads, causing unnecessary network traffic and increased latency.\n\nThis work addresses image sharing inefficiency across containers in multiple VMs on a bare-metal server by leveraging SmartNICs\u2014specialized network hardware that accelerates and offloads networking tasks. By integrating SmartNIC capabilities, the proposed method optimizes image retrieval, enabling more efficient sharing of container images between containers running on different VMs within the same bare-metal container environment.\n\nThe approach demonstrates significant performance improvements, reducing container cold start times by up to 92% and cutting network traffic by 99.9%. Moreover, these benefits scale with the number of VMs concurrently accessing the same container image on the bare-metal server, ensuring increased efficiency as server specifications advance. Thus, the solution enhances the utilization of bare-metal container infrastructure by improving inter-VM container image sharing without compromising VM isolation, ultimately advancing the performance and scalability of containerized applications in cloud data centers.",

Results demonstrate that around 10 mM H2O2 significantly delays leaf yellowing, reducing the yellowing rate by 8.2% and 26.4% after 4 and 8 days of storage, respectively, compared to untreated controls. Moreover, oxidative stress in Chinese cabbage leaves was mitigated by suppression of respiratory burst oxidase homologs and upregulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging genes. This antioxidative response was further supported by reduced lipid peroxidation and preservation of cell integrity and photochemical efficiency in treated leaves.\n\nOverall, preharvest H2O2 application on Chinese cabbage leaves activates antioxidant defense systems, protects chloroplast membranes from oxidative damage, limits water loss, and ultimately delays leaf senescence during postharvest storage. This study expanded on that research by analyzing 52 diverse maize genotypes, examining mineral and phytate concentrations and iron bioavailability before (whole kernels) and after degermination.\n\nWhole and degerminated maize samples were cooked, dried, and milled into corn flour. Iron bioavailability was assessed using an in vitro digestion Caco2 cell bioassay. Results showed that in 30 genotypes, iron bioavailability increased post-degermination, despite iron concentrations dropping by over 70% when the germ fraction was removed. This indicates higher fractional iron uptake in these corn varieties after degermination. In contrast, 22 genotypes exhibited either no change or a decrease in iron bioavailability following degermination. These findings confirm that the germ fraction in corn acts as a strong inhibitor of iron absorption in many maize types.\n\nPhytate concentrations in corn flours were significantly reduced by degermination; however, the relationship between phytate levels and iron bioavailability is complex. Depending on corn kernel color and the processing method used to produce the flour, phytate can either inhibit or promote iron uptake. Additionally, other factors in the corn endosperm, such as vitreous versus floury composition and bran polyphenol content, likely influence iron bioavailability after degermination.\n\nOverall, this study shows that iron nutrition from corn can be improved by selecting maize genotypes in which the inhibitory effects of bran color and endosperm characteristics are minimized, particularly after processing through degermination. Thus, degermination, in combination with targeted genotype selection, offers an effective approach to enhance iron bioavailability in corn-based foods.",

"http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/AfPO_0000494": "The text discusses the presence of a series of dental obstruents in certain Bantu languages of northeastern Kenya, specifically highlighting Pokomo alongside northern Swahili dialects and Elwana. Unlike Proto-Bantu and most East African Bantu languages, which lack such dental series, these languages have developed them through distinct mechanisms. Three primary processes are identified: (a) the incorporation of sounds via loan vocabulary, (b) a straightforward phonological shift where inherited alveolar consonants shifted to dental positions, and (c) a more complex shift where inherited (pre) palatal sounds bypassed alveolars to become dental, a relatively rare occurrence in linguistic literature. The development of these dental sounds, as present in Pokomo and neighboring languages, is hypothesized to have resulted from historical contact with neighboring Cushitic communities. Notably, the contact was not with the large modern Eastern Cushitic groups like Somali or Orma, but rather with ancestral and remnant languages, possibly including Southern Cushitic Dahalo and Eastern Cushitic Aweera. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03500015": "This work presents a general approach to fabricating superhydrophobic coatings solely from food-grade wax surfaces and solvents, emphasizing sustainability and safety for applications such as food packaging. Utilizing dispersions composed of only two components\u2014a food-grade wax and a solvent\u2014the method exploits variations in wax solubility and dispersibility during solvent exchange to produce coatings with water contact angles (WCAs) exceeding 150\u00b0, confirming their superhydrophobic nature. These food-grade wax surface coatings are prepared by mixing formulations at room and elevated temperatures (above wax melting points), followed by spray coating onto substrates like glass and cardboard.\n\nThe study highlights that the best-performing food-grade wax surfaces, such as rice bran wax dispersed in n-hexane, achieve the highest surface roughness, resulting in WCAs around 156\u00b0 and water sliding angles below 10\u00b0. Importantly, the food-grade wax surface coatings demonstrate remarkable stability, maintaining superhydrophobicity over extended storage times and resisting water submersion for up to 24 hours. Conventional desalination methods are unsustainable due to their high energy needs and chemical usage. An emerging alternative is the adsorption cycle for desalination, which operates at suitable temperatures and offers advantages such as better integration synergy to boost performance. However, conventional adsorption (AD) cycle processes face challenges, including inefficient adsorbent packing and heat transfer losses in large heat exchangers, limiting their efficiency.\n\nThis study proposes an innovative pressure-driven adsorption (PDAD) cycle to address these limitations. The proposed system achieves excellent thermodynamic synergy when integrated with combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) power and desalination plants, enabling more efficient use of low-pressure bleed steam. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03541034": "\u00a9 2025 xu et al. this is an open access article distributed under the terms of the creative commons attribution license, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited.soil contamination by heavy metals presents substantial ecological and geotechnical risks, thereby demanding sustainable remediation strategies. conventional approaches, including chemical stabilization and microbial-induced carbonate precipitation (micp), are limited by high costs, ecological disturbances, and sensitivity to environmental stressors. a plant-derived urease-driven enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (eicp) system was evaluated for immobilizing cadmium (cd2+), lead (pb2+), and zinc (zn2+) in contaminated soils. systematic screening revealed that jack bean and watermelon seed ureases are optimal catalysts for heavy metal sequestration, achieving efficiencies of 87.3% for cd2 + , 91.5% for pb2 + , and 76.4% for zn2 + . these high efficiencies are attributed to their catalytic specificity and the retained enzymatic activity under environmental stress. critical process parameters were fine-tuned through iterative experimentation, maintaining a urea-cacl2 reaction stoichiometry of 1.5:1 molar ratio and calibrating the enzyme dosage to 1.2 u/g of soil matrix. this optimized operational range effectively promoted carbonate mineralization while preserving essential soil hydraulic properties, as evidenced by sustained permeability exceeding 10 - 5 cm/s throughout precipitation cycles. durability assessments under simulated acid rain and freeze-thaw cycles demonstrated 82.5% retention of cd2+ and 92.7% retention of unconfined compressive strength, outperforming conventional lime and micp treatments. x-ray diffraction analysis confirmed the presence of stable crystalline phases. field validation confirmed that the eicp protocol can be feasibly scaled to real-world sites with operational costs averaging $52 per cubic meter, representing a 61% reduction compared to microbial-based treatments. this plant-based eicp approach offers a scalable and cost-effective solution for ecological restoration and geotechnical stabilization in contaminated soils, demonstrating significant potential for sustainable environmental management.",

The presence of lime also substantially enhances hydrochar yield derived from sugar beet pulp, reaching 68.8% compared to 27.4% when using KOH. Although AHA production is lower with lime (3.47%) relative to KOH (15.50%), the lime-treated hydrothermal products are enriched in calcium and magnesium and maintain a neutral pH of 7. This composition suggests that lime-treated sugar beet pulp hydrothermal fertilizers are safer and more efficient alternatives.\n\nCharacterization of AHAs derived from sugar beet pulp via lime-assisted HTH corresponds well with natural humic substances, supporting their beneficial role in soil amendment. Application of these lime-processed products at 0.01% w/w significantly improves wheat growth and nutrient uptake over controls, without exhibiting toxicity towards Daphnia magna. Overall, this research highlights the potential of sugar beet pulp as a sustainable feedstock for producing eco-friendly, calcium- and magnesium-rich hydrothermal fertilizers through lime-assisted HTH, advancing the development of novel agricultural inputs.",

Plant roots generally decompose more slowly than shoots and contribute more significantly to soil organic matter accumulation, while soil management history can shape decomposer communities and nutrient cycling.\n\nIn the experiment, radish plant shoots and roots were incubated for 180 days at 20\u00b0C in four different soils distinguished by management histories: organic versus mineral fertilisation, and with or without prior cover crop (CC) use. The release of carbon (C) as CO2 and extractable mineral nitrogen (N) was measured to assess mineralisation rates.\n\nInitial results showed that more C from radish shoots was mineralised than from radish roots during the first 10 days of incubation. After 180 days, 58% of the total C input from radish plant material was mineralised, with no significant difference between radish shoots and roots. Regarding nitrogen, radish shoots released a higher proportion of N (42% of shoot N) compared to radish roots (28% of root N) by the end of incubation.\n\nSoil management history did not influence net mineralisation of radish plant C; however, soils with a history of cover crop use exhibited enhanced net N mineralisation from radish residues. This suggests that long-term C decomposition from radish plant shoots and roots is unaffected by their chemical differences or soil management regime, whereas N mineralisation rates vary depending on both radish plant organ and soil history.\n\nIn summary, while the chemical characteristics of radish plant shoots and roots do not affect the overall carbon mineralisation after long-term incubation, nitrogen mineralisation occurs faster in radish shoots than in roots and is enhanced in soils previously managed with cover crops. Avocado oil contains notably higher levels of cis-vaccenic acid, typically ranging from 5.5% to 7.5% of total fatty acids, whereas high oleic sunflower oil contains less than 1.3% and high oleic safflower oil less than 0.75%. Incorporating such a standard would enhance the ability to identify avocado oil adulteration, ensuring greater purity and quality assurance in the market. Research aiming to study gene expression alongside pork quality indices benefits from collecting adipose and muscle tissue samples from the same anatomical location of an individual animal. Typically, tissue samples are collected immediately after exsanguination to maximize RNA integrity, crucial for sensitive RNA-based assays like real-time PCR. However, collecting samples at this time requires cutting through the hide, leaving underlying tissue exposed during food scalding, which poses potential food safety risks and may confound pork quality measurements.\n\nTo address these issues related to food scalding, a study investigated the effect of tissue sampling timing post-harvest\u2014specifically following exsanguination, food scalding, or chilling\u2014on RNA integrity, real-time PCR results, and pork quality. The study found that sampling time did not affect RNA quality, as measured by RNA integrity number (RIN) in both adipose and muscle tissues. Similarly, real-time PCR gene expression results were not influenced when comparing samples taken immediately following exsanguination or after food scalding.\n\nHowever, tissue sampled prior to food scalding showed significant differences in pork color attributes, including a higher visual color score and lower L* and b* values, although 24-hour pH remained unaffected. These findings suggest that tissue sampling after food scalding and dehairing can be performed without compromising RNA integrity or altering gene expression results from real-time PCR assays. Moreover, delaying sampling until after food scalding associates with minimal impact on pork quality measurements.\n\nIn conclusion, to study both RNA-based assays and meat quality within the same anatomical location, tissue sampling should occur immediately following food scalding. This approach mitigates food safety concerns linked to exposed tissue during scalding, ensures reliable RNA integrity for molecular assays, and minimizes alterations in pork quality metrics. Thus, integrating tissue sampling post food scalding represents an effective strategy for advancing sustainable pork production research.",

Broiler chickens are recognized as the main reservoirs of these pathogens, and outbreaks are mainly linked to the consumption of raw or undercooked poultry meat. Historically, *C. jejuni* has been the dominant species detected in chicken meat, accounting for over 80% of campylobacteriosis cases, with *C. coli* responsible for about 10%. However, recent findings show an increasing prevalence of *C. coli* in chicken meat, sometimes even surpassing *C. jejuni* as the dominant species.\n\nThe review emphasizes the complexity of studying *Campylobacter* prevalence in poultry, particularly in samples such as chicken leg (skinless), which represents a crucial part of the broiler carcass commonly analyzed in surveillance and research. Factors influencing detection include the sampling method (e.g., swabs, carcass rinsates, or excised skinless meat samples like those from the chicken leg), the specific carcass part sampled (neck, breast, or leg), and environmental conditions like seasonality (summer versus winter) and farm-level parameters (rainfall, humidity).\n\nOther determinants discussed involve laboratory procedures including the isolation techniques (enumeration versus detection), pathogen identification methods (biochemical or molecular), and the selective media used for culturing (e.g., Bolton or Preston broths, and charcoal-based or chromogenic agars). The biofilm-forming capacity of different *Campylobacter* strains further contributes to their persistence and prevalence in poultry meat products such as chicken leg (skinless).\n\nThis detailed review highlights the multifaceted nature of *Campylobacter* contamination in chicken meat, with a particular focus on chicken leg (skinless) samples, reflecting both epidemiological shifts in species distribution and methodological variables essential for accurate detection and understanding of *Campylobacter* prevalence in the poultry industry.",

"http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03530150": "The study investigates Ordovician oolitic iron formations in eastern Alborz, Iran, focusing on their mineralogical and geochemical characteristics, genesis, and economic significance. Oolitic iron formations are sedimentary rocks containing over 5 vol.% oolites and more than 15 wt.% iron (21.4 wt.% Fe2O3) (Young, 1989; Petranek and Van Houten, 1997; Mucke and Farshad, 2005). Samples from the Lashkarak Formation's Abarsej, Dehmola, and Simehkuh sections were analyzed using petrographic, XRD, XRF, ICP-ES, and SEM methods.\n\nThe oolitic iron formations are mainly hosted by carbonate argillites and are rich in chamositic and hematitic oolites with minor goethite, pyrite, and glauconite; siderite is absent. Geochemically, total FeO (TFeO) ranges from 8% to 48%, averaging 21%. Based on TFeO content, two groups are defined: low-grade iron formations (Abarsej section) with TFeO < 23%, high MgO (0.82\u20130.96%), and high CaO (33\u201337%), and high-grade iron formations (Dehmola and Simehkuh sections) with TFeO between 23% and 48%, low MgO (0.03\u20130.1%), and high TiO2 (1.46\u20132.21%). The classification into low-grade and high-grade iron formations aligns with mineralogical differences: low-grade types contain chamosite and calcite, whereas high-grade types consist mainly of hematite and calcite.\n\nThe origin of iron in these oolitic formations is linked to normal seawater Fe availability, with Fe transported as clastic particles or coatings derived from weathered shales. The presence of K, Si, detrital zircon, quartz, and clay minerals supports a genesis involving Fe-bearing clays under medium-weak redox conditions (pH 5\u20139) (Maynard, 1983, 1986). Diagenetic transformation of chamosite and goethite to hematite explains the abundance of hematite and dense oolite textures.\n\nFindings suggest that the studied members currently represent low-grade oolitic iron formations (average 21 wt.% Fe) without notable economic importance. While references to \u201cgrade a\u201d and \u201cEurope\u201d are implicit through citations\u2014particularly Young (1989), who studied Ordovician oolitic ironstones in Western Europe\u2014this research focuses on Iranian deposits, contributing to the broader understanding of oolitic ironstone formation and classification globally.",

However, increasing the cold plate inlet flow rate from 0.2 L/min to 1 L/min and lowering the inlet temperature from 24 \u00b0C to 15 \u00b0C both significantly reduced the total thermal resistance. Notably, while increasing flow rate decreased the rate of pressure increase with heat removal, lowering the cold plate inlet temperature did not affect this pressure-rate relationship.\n\nThese results were effectively captured by a simple analytical model with one adjusted free parameter\u2014accounting for increased thermal resistance of the heat sink at low flow rates. In the Boro site, species richness was significantly higher within 0\u201310 m from surface water compared to greater distances, and species diversity was also elevated closer to the water. The Jao and Upper Panhandle sites showed significant differences in basal area, with Jao displaying greater basal area closer to surface water (0\u201310 m). Canopy cover varied significantly with distance at all Okavango sites studied. Moreover, plant species composition shifted noticeably along the gradient away from surface water within each site.\n\nGLM results indicated that both site and distance from surface water played significant roles in shaping species diversity and basal area in the Okavango Delta, while species richness and cover were more strongly influenced by site alone. These findings highlight that distance from surface water and site-specific conditions are important determinants of riparian vegetation dynamics in the Okavango Delta. This improved understanding aids in informing wetland management policies aimed at conserving the unique biodiversity and ecological functioning of the Okavango Delta wetlands.",

exploitation. the cost of drying, storage, and transport poses additional economical limitations to waste utilization. therefore, agroindustrial waste often is utilized as feed or fertilizer. however, demand for feed or fertilizer varies and depends on agricultural production. moreover, valuable nutrients contained in agroindustrial wastes are lost. thus new aspects concerning the use of these wastes as by-products for further exploitation on the production of food additives or supplements with high nutritional value have gained increasing interest because these are high-value products and their recovery may be economically attractive. it is well known that agroindustrial by-products are rich in dietary fibers, some of which contain appreciable amounts of colorants, antioxidant compounds or other substances with positive health effects, while some of them, like the oilseed meals, are rich in proteins. dietary fibers consist of polysaccharides and lignin that are neither digested nor absorbed in the human small intestine. the beneficial role of dietary fibers in reducing risk of coronary heart disease and certain types of cancer has been pointed out by several epidemiological studies. the recommended daily intake is 30-45 g per day and person, while the estimated consumption in the west is about 20 g per day and person (thebaudin et al., 1997). cereals make up to 35- 60% of the actual consumption while fruits and vegetables contribute only 7-15% (grigelmo-miguel and martin-belloso, 1999b). cereals are rich in insoluble dietary fibers, which are mainly related to intestinal regulation, while fruits and vegetables contain appreciable amounts of soluble dietary fibers, which help in lowering blood cholesterol and glucose intestinal absorption. soluble dietary fibers should account for 30-50% of the total dietary fibers intake to improve dietary benefits. apart from health effects dietary fibers show some functional properties, such as water-holding capacity, swelling capacity, increasing viscosity or gel formation which are essential in formulating certain food products. formulated food products with high dietary fibers content are now commercially available. dietary fibers incorporated in these products are obtained mainly by cereals. citrus and apple pomace are also raw materials for the production of dietary fiber powders. activity in vitro and in vivo (kiokias and gordon 2004). polyphenols also act as antioxidants; they scavenge free radicals which are responsible for serious diseases and for the oxidation of lipids, proteins, and dna. several studies have revealed their antimicrobial, antithrombotic, antimutagenic, and anticarcinogenic activities (kandaswami and middleton, 1997; sahu and green, 1997). in addition to health benefits, the supplementation of food products with antioxidants delays the formation of off-flavors and rancidity and extends the shelf life of the product. carotenoids and polyphenols are extensively distributed in several plant by-products. thus most fruit and vegetable by-products could serve as raw materials for their recovery. moreover, these antioxidants or colorants would have a natural origin, which is in accordance with the demands of consumers for \"all natural\" because of the possible toxicity of synthetic additives. the role for food proteins in human nutrition is substantial, while according to modern nutrition recommendations the supply of proteins in human diet should rely mostly on vegetable proteins, i.e., cereals, legumes, oilseeds, etc., than on those from animal sources, i.e., meat. because the amounts of proteins required to cover the nutritional needs of the world population are continuously increasing, the investigation and finding of new protein sources are of interest. in addition to their nutritional value, proteins offer great potential as functional food ingredients providing useful properties when incorporated into foods. in order to utilize a byproduct as a protein source it should both present high protein content and protein value (quality) based on well-balanced essential amino acids. an additional requirement to utilize a material for food purposes is the absence of allergic or toxic substances or the application of a proper pretreatment for their efficient removal. several protein products (flours, concentrates, or isolates), depending on their protein content, can be introduced to food products in order to improve their nutritional value as well as their sensory and functional properties. such protein products already have been used as meat extenders in processed meat products or as protein-enriching agents in nutritional beverages. particularly, soy protein products are used for the production of several foods such as: imitation cheese, whipped toppings, soy milk, and baked products. today consumers are highly aware of the close relationship between nutrition and health and they want to include health-promoting ingredients in their diets. foods fortified with nutraceuticals, or functional foods in other terms, are expected to be the new food category with an expanding demand by future generations. therefore, food scientists focus their effort on the development of new products with improved nutritional profiles. natural ingredients recovered from agroindustrial by-products have specific dietary and functional properties and can be utilized effectively to develop this new food category.",

reaction against the authority of the roman catholic church. this process led to radical changes in christianity\u2019s history, reshaping the religio-cultural landscape of today\u2019s europe. therefore, the reformation was more than a religious movement; it was a turning point that radically changed europe\u2019s social, political and cultural structure. during the reformation period, protestant reformists criticized the institutional structure and theological doctrines of the roman catholic church. one primary criticism was the church\u2019s doctrine of interpreting miracles as a manifestation of its own perfection, and presenting saints and their relics as ongoing sources of miraculous events. leading reformists rejected these claims as running contrary to the bible. they interpreted miracles within their own paradigms. martin luther, for instance, regarded them as an indication of god\u2019s power, associating them with faith. huldreich zwingli attributed an allegorical meaning to miracles that focused more on their moral and spiritual messages. similarly, john calvin added a more profound meaning to miracles, and accepted them as a sign of god\u2019s sovereignty, arguing that they were limited to the apostolic period. he differed from luther by stating that while miracles occurred in the past to affirm god\u2019s message, basing faith on miracles was no longer appropriate. therefore, these reformists lacked a consensus on miracles by criticizing and rejecting the church\u2019s understanding of them. regarding the sacrament of the eucharist, an important miracle according to the roman catholic church, luther argued that christ was physically present in the eucharist, while zwingli interpreted this presence symbolically. calvin, on the other hand, evaluated christ\u2019s presence in the eucharist spiritually. concerning the possibility of miracles today, luther believed them to be possible, albeit unnecessary for salvation. however, zwingli argued that miracles no longer occurred. calvin aligned with zwingli, asserting god remained active in the world not through miracles, but through the holy spirit. these differences are important, as they reflect each reformer\u2019s theological approaches, their commitment to christian tradition, and their interpretations of sacred texts. over time, however, these followers of these reformers formed distinct theological schools (e.g., lutheranism and calvinism), each offering myriad understandings of miracles. by examining how reformist texts approached miracles, this study seeks to shed light on their impact on the christian understanding of miracles. although the reformation has been studied widely, no direct study has been conducted in t\u00fcrkiye on the metaphorical aspect of miracles from this period. furthermore, no comprehensive study in reformation theology has explored the concept of miracles or the views of early reformers on this topic. to address this gap, the present study explores how leading reformers conceptualized miracles and how they understood their theological significance. specifically, it examines the impact of these thinkers on the christian understanding of miracles. this study contributes to the theological corpus on the reformation and offers insight for interdisciplinary and interreligious scholarship aimed at understanding diverse perspectives on supernatural phenomena. it occupies a significant place in the literature by analyzing the influence of the reformist ideas on modern christian theology and practices. the reformers\u2019 understanding of miracles will be subjected to a phenomenological comparison. the study will also employ a sociological approach to understand the period\u2019s social structure, and the extent to which belief in miracles influenced it. in particular, the study will examine the reformists\u2019 efforts to interpret biblical miracle narratives and to transform texts into a doctrine. this study is primarily based on theological sources from the reformation period and the writings of leading reformists. the article also aims to clarify the meaning of the concept of miracle within reformed theology and to assess the extent to which early reformists\u2019 interpretations align the traditional christian understanding. as the first academic study in t\u00fcrkiye on this subject, it is expected to lay the groundwork for future research. moreover, comparing how leading reformists understand miracles is crucial for grasping the depth of theological debates during the reformation, and how different interpretations of christianity were shaped. this comparison also sheds light on the diversity of reformation-era theology and the evolution of christian approaches to miracles. the study finds both similarities and differences in the reformists\u2019 understanding of miracles. these differing approaches make the christian concept of miracles more universal by placing it within a historical and theological framework, thereby enriching the existing body of theological and philosophical literature on miracles in christianity.",

"http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_02022328": "The giant liver fluke, Fascioloides magna, is implicated as a potential factor in moose (Alces alces) population declines in North America, though direct evidence linking F. magna infection to moose mortality remains limited. This review highlights significant knowledge gaps concerning the transmission dynamics and impact of F. magna on moose liver health and overall moose populations. It emphasizes the need for further research into the ecological role of the intermediate snail hosts in the parasite's life cycle, which have been largely overlooked in current management strategies. These intermediate hosts for F. magna appear to vary regionally, with genetic studies suggesting that F. magna was confined to isolated refugia during historic cervid extirpation periods in North America. This historical distribution poses important coevolutionary and pathological implications for definitive hosts, including how F. magna infections might affect moose liver condition. The review proposes that F. magna infections may be most significant in moose through sublethal effects and in the context of co-infections, influencing moose liver health and fitness rather than causing direct mortality. Current landscape-scale risk models predominantly rely on white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) as monitoring hosts, which only indirectly measure infection risk to moose liver health and related declines. Incorporating data on snail habitat availability, especially in ephemeral wetlands, could improve model accuracy and better predict F. magna transmission risk to moose liver and populations. In particular, the standard Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation is inapplicable to such matrices due to their heavy-tailed nature.\n\nTo overcome this challenge, the authors employ the functional Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation, enabling an exact analytical treatment in the limit of large matrix sizes. Thus, the L\u00e9vy-Rosenzweig-Porter random matrices provide a rich model for investigating spectral properties and phase behavior in systems with heavy-tailed disorder.\n\nIn summary, by applying the functional Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation within Efetov's supersymmetric formalism, the work achieves an analytical solution for the spectral density in L\u00e9vy and L\u00e9vy-Rosenzweig-Porter random matrix ensembles. These histozoic parasites cause enteromyxosis in intensive finfish aquaculture. Transmission between fish in net-pen systems occurs via epicellular and sloughed histozoic stages, while actinospores from an annelid host are believed necessary for infection of wild fish. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03310333": "The text presents the first comprehensive theory of glacier surging that incorporates both temperate and polythermal glacier surges, grounded in coupled mass and enthalpy budgets. Enthalpy, encompassing thermal energy and glacier water, is gained at the glacier bed through geothermal and frictional heating caused by ice flow. Losses of enthalpy occur via conduction and the loss of meltwater (glacier water) from the system. Since enthalpy directly influences glacier flow speeds, maintaining steady glacier flow requires simultaneous balancing of mass and enthalpy budgets. Failure to maintain this balance results in out-of-phase mass and enthalpy cycles, leading to alternating quiescent and surge phases in glaciers.\n\nA lumped element model illustrates the theory by parameterizing key thermodynamic and hydrological processes, including surface-to-bed drainage as well as distributed and channelized drainage systems involving glacier water. The model reproduces many observed features of polythermal and temperate glacier surges, highlighting how surging behavior is linked to specific combinations of climate factors (precipitation and temperature), glacier geometry (length and slope), and bed properties such as hydraulic conductivity, which affect the movement and storage of glacier water.\n\nThis enthalpy balance theory integrates glacier water dynamics into the broader understanding of glacier surging, explaining a wide range of observed surging behaviors within a unified framework. It offers insight into the fundamental role of glacier water, alongside thermal energy, in controlling flow variations. Ultimately, the theory helps answer why the majority of glaciers do not surge, emphasizing the critical influence of glacier water and enthalpy processes on glacier stability and dynamics.",

"http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_00002891": "This text discusses allergy to chicken egg proteins, emphasizing the role of molecular diagnostics in managing chicken egg allergy. The main allergenic proteins identified in chicken egg include ovomucoid (Gal d 1), ovalbumin (Gal d 2), ovotransferrin (Gal d 3), A-livetin (Gal d 5), and lysozyme (Gal d 4). This distinction is crucial when considering dietary options for individuals with chicken egg allergy.\n\nTo diagnose allergies to chicken egg proteins, methods such as skin prick tests and measurement of antigen-specific immunoglobulins E are used. However, the most definitive confirmation remains the double-blind food challenge test. Molecular diagnostics enable the identification of specific allergenic molecules in chicken egg, such as ovomucoid, ovalbumin, or ovotransferrin, allowing for refined allergy assessment.\n\nWith these diagnostic tools, it is possible to better manage chicken egg allergy by controlling hypersensitivity symptoms and tailoring elimination diets. Since egg yolk provides valuable amino acids and fats, confirming tolerance to chicken egg (baked) can aid in nutritional planning, preventing unnecessary restrictions. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03411345": "Cells of spent brewer's yeast represent a natural and sustainable material for encapsulating aroma compounds. While the use of yeast cells as microcapsules has been proven decades ago, the corresponding technologies have yet to gain industrial traction. This is partly due to the conventional production method, which involves suspending yeast cells and aroma oil in water, resulting in mixtures with poor processability. Such limitations likely contribute to the lack of market-established applications for yeast-based encapsulation. Alternatively, production of flavor-filled yeast cells without the suspension step is achievable using concentrated powder form technology. In the described work, a high-pressure spraying process was employed to fabricate a dry powder of yeast cells containing 15 wt% limonene. The release behavior of these yeast capsules was studied in various model matrices to evaluate their potential application in food products. Results demonstrated that the release of aroma compounds from yeast cells could be immediate or prolonged, depending on the composition of the surrounding media, with water confirmed as the primary trigger for release. Overall, the fabricated yeast capsules demonstrate promise as a controlled release system, leveraging the natural properties of yeast cells to encapsulate and release flavor compounds effectively.",

Both passives share the feature that the oblique case of a passivized object noun phrase (NP) is preserved. Recent surveys indicate that Icelandic speakers who accept the Reflexive Passive do not necessarily accept the New Passive. However, the reverse is true: those who accept the New Passive also accept the Reflexive Passive. This pattern has led to the proposal of a Passive Acceptability Hierarchy specific to Icelandic, reflecting varying degrees of acceptance among speakers for different passive constructions.\n\nThe validity of this hierarchy in Icelandic is further supported by a diachronic corpus study using open access digital texts from Icelandic journals and newspapers spanning the 19th and 20th centuries, accessible via the t\u00edmarit.is digital library. This historical analysis provides empirical evidence for the evolving acceptance patterns of passive forms in Icelandic over time.\n\nThe authors propose an analysis of the Reflexive Passive in Icelandic grounded in argument structure. They argue that the differences in acceptability between the Reflexive Passive and the New Passive in Icelandic arise from the argument status of the object involved. Specifically, simplex reflexive pronouns in Icelandic are semantically dependent on their selecting verbs and should consequently be treated as syntactic arguments rather than semantic arguments of these verbs. This distinction is central to understanding why the Reflexive Passive enjoys distinct acceptability patterns compared to the New Passive in Icelandic.\n\nIn summary, the study highlights nuanced passive constructions in Icelandic, revealing a hierarchy of acceptability and offering a syntactic-semantic explanation for variation in speaker judgments. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000191": "inter- and circumstellar ices comprise different molecules accreted on cold dust particles. these icy dust grains provide a molecule reservoir where particles can interact and react. as the grain acts as a third body, capable of absorbing energy, icy surfaces in space have a catalytic effect. chemical reactions are triggered by a number of possible processes; (i) irradiation by light, typically uv photons from the interstellar radiation field and ly-\u03b1 radiation emitted by excited hydrogen, but also x-rays, (ii) bombardment by particles, free atoms (most noticeably hydrogen, but also n, c, o and d-atoms), electrons, low energy ions and cosmic rays, and (iii) thermal processing. all these effects cause ices to (photo)desorb, induce fragmentation or ionization in the ice, and eventual recombination will make molecules to react and to form more and more complex species. the effects of this solid state astrochemistry are observed by astronomers; nearly 180 different molecules (not including isotopologues) have been unambiguously identified in the inter- and circumstellar medium, and the abundances of a substantial part of these species cannot be explained by gas phase reaction schemes only and must involve solid state chemistry. icy dust grains in space experience different chemical stages. in the diffuse medium grains are barely covered by molecules, but upon gravitational collapse and darkening of the cloud, temperatures drop and dust grains start acting as micrometer sized cryopumps. more and more species accrete, until even the most volatile species are frozen. in parallel (non)energetic processing can take place, particularly during planet and star formation when radiation and particle fluxes are intense. the physical and chemical properties of ice clearly provide a snapshotroot to characterize the cosmological chemical evolution. in order to fully interpret the astronomical observations, therefore, dedicated laboratory experiments are needed that simulate dust grain formation and processing as well as ice mantle chemistry under astronomical conditions and in full control of the relevant parameters; ice morphology (i.e., structure), composition, temperature, uv and particle fluxes, etc., yielding parameters that can be used for astrochemical modeling and for comparison with the observations. this is the topic of the present manuscript. laboratory experiments simulating the conditions in space are conducted for decades all over the world, but particularly in recent years new techniques have made it possible to study reactions involving inter- and circumstellar dust and ice analogues at an unprecedented level of detail. whereas in the past \"top-down scenarios\" allowed to conclude on the importance of the solid state for the chemical enrichment of space, presently \"bottom-up approaches\" make it possible to fully quantify the involved reactions, and to provide information on processes at the molecular level. the recent progress in the field of \"solid state laboratory astrophysics\" is a consequence of the use of ultra high vacuum systems, of new radiation sources, such as synchrotrons and laser systems that allow extensions to wavelength domains that long have not been accessible, including the thz domain, and the use of highly sensitive gas phase detection techniques, explicitly applied to characterize the solid state such as fluorescence, luminescence, cavity ring-down spectroscopy and sophisticated mass spectrometric techniques. this paper presents an overview of the techniques being used in astrochemical laboratories worldwide, but it is incomplete in the sense that it summarizes the outcome of a 3-day workshop of the authors in november 2012 (at the observatoire de meudon in france), with several laboratories represented, but not all. the paper references earlier work, but it is incomplete with regard to latest developments of techniques used in laboratories not represented at the workshop. \u00a9 2013 springer science+business media dordrecht.",

These findings provide a comprehensive understanding of the drying kinetics and mass transfer mechanisms involved in pineapple (dried) processing within a closed-loop heat pump drying system.\n\nThis research contributes valuable insights for optimizing energy-efficient drying processes of pineapple (dried) slices, promoting improved product quality and process control.\n\nReference: Tun\u00e7kal, C., Co\u015fkun, S., Doymaz, I., & Ergun, E. and sluice gates has disconnected most of these lakes from the main channel of the yangtze river, preventing c. nasus from spawning and rearing offspring. in the chaohu lake, the primary river-connected channel has been equipped with sluice gates, resulting in the lake disconnected from the yangtze river, and the population of c. nasus in chaohu lake being classified as landlocked. ecological types of c. nasus in chaohu lake and tracing their origins can enhance our understanding of its migratory ecology and provide a more comprehensive view of lake connectivity, improving our ability to protect the ecology of chaohu lake. in july 2022, nine adult c. nasus samples were collected from chaohu lake in the anhui province, china. in this study, the otolith sr/ca ratio was returned to freshwater, reflecting a migratory life history. the 87sr/86sr ratios of the otoliths of 22ch07 were initially high at 0.71451, corresponding to the region with high sr/ca ratios and This investigation marks the initial confirmation of domoic acid presence linked to amnesic shellfish poisoning in Croatian waters, contributing critical data for monitoring and managing ASP risks in shellfish harvesting areas. Forward thrust during both upstroke and downstroke was rare and only observed in hatchlings exhibiting the biphasic pattern, thus the third hypothesis was only occasionally supported. In contrast, n-hexane extracts of Roselle calyx showed no antibacterial activity. Fungal biomass reduction varied with solvent extraction; the greatest suppression of fungal growth occurred with 80% n-hexane Roselle calyx extracts, while 60% methanol extracts resulted in the least reduction.\n\nA significant negative correlation (r = \u22120.882; p < 0.05) was found between the IC50 values in the DPPH antioxidant assay and total phenolic content of Roselle calyx extracts, underscoring the strong relationship between antioxidant activity and phenolic compounds. These findings suggest that the choice of extraction solvent critically influences the yield of bioactive compounds and corresponding biological activities in Roselle calyx.\n\nOverall, this study highlights the promising antioxidant and antimicrobial properties of Roselle calyx, particularly in methanolic extracts, and emphasizes the need for further research to fully explore Roselle calyx\u2019s potential in natural medicine, nutrition, functional foods, and therapeutic applications.",

The two primary species found in chicken meat are *Campylobacter jejuni* and *Campylobacter coli*, causing nearly 90% of reported human cases\u2014over 80% from *C. jejuni* and about 10% from *C. coli*. While *C. jejuni* has traditionally been recognized as the dominant species in chicken meat, recent evidence indicates a rising prevalence of *C. coli*, sometimes surpassing *C. jejuni* in dominance.  \n\nThis epidemiological shift is examined within the context of various factors impacting the detection and prevalence of *Campylobacter* spp. in chicken meat samples, including those taken specifically from the poultry neck (raw). Sampling methods such as swabs or rinsates, the part of the carcass sampled (neck, breast, leg), and whether samples are skinned or skinless significantly influence detection outcomes. The poultry neck (raw), as a distinct anatomical site, is a focus due to its relevance in both contamination risk and variation in bacterial load. Furthermore, seasonal variation (summer versus winter), environmental conditions at the farm level (rainfall, humidity), and laboratory procedures\u2014including isolation techniques, enrichment media choice, and pathogen identification approaches\u2014add layers of complexity to understanding *Campylobacter* prevalence.\n\nThe review also considers microbial characteristics such as biofilm-forming ability, which affects survival and persistence on poultry products like the raw neck portion. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03414816": "The Bogong moth (Agrotis infusa) is a notable Australian insect renowned for its impressive nocturnal navigation abilities. Similar to the Monarch butterflies of North America, Bogong moths undertake an annual long-distance migration from southern Queensland, western and northwestern New South Wales (NSW), and western Victoria to the alpine regions of NSW and Victoria. Emerging from their pupae in early spring, adult Bogong moths embark on a nocturnal journey that can span over 1000 km and take days or weeks.\n\nUpon reaching the Australian Alps by late September, Bogong moths seek refuge in specific high-elevation caves and rock crevices, typically above 1800 meters. Here, in vast numbers, they line the cave walls and enter a state of summer dormancy known as estivation. By late summer (February and March), the same Bogong moth individuals leave these estivation sites and commence their return to breeding grounds. There, they mate, lay eggs, and subsequently die. The offspring that hatch the next spring repeat the migratory cycle.\n\nRemarkably, Bogong moths successfully navigate to the alpine estivation sites despite having no prior experience of the migratory route. The precise mechanisms underlying this migratory feat remain unclear, though it is hypothesized that Bogong moths use a combination of sensory cues\u2014visual, olfactory, mechanical, and magnetic\u2014along their journey.\n\nThis text reviews the Bogong moth\u2019s natural history, ecology, and cultural significance to Australian Aboriginal peoples. Further, it highlights the Bogong moth as a promising new model organism for scientific research into the sensory basis of nocturnal insect migration. Understanding how Bogong moths accomplish their long-distance nocturnal migration offers valuable insights into insect navigation and sensory biology.",

Additionally, color stability and flavor retention in the finished product are critical, especially for grape juice, wine, and jelly cultivars. These requirements help maintain the quality and marketability of wine jelly and other grape-based products. This overview aims to inform county extension agents, extension faculty, grape growers, homeowners, and students interested in grape cultivation in Florida about the characteristics needed for successful commercial fresh market, wine, juice, and jelly grape cultivars. Detailed information about grape production adaptations in Florida is available at https://hos.ifas.ufl.edu/grape/. The previously referenced work by Breman and Andersen (2009, updated 2018) titled \u201cCommercial Fresh Market, Wine, Juice, and Jelly Grape Cultivars for Florida\u201d (EDIS 2018 (3), HS1152/HS401) provides a foundational resource on this topic (https://doi.org/10.32473/edis-hs401-2008). Notably, cloisonne kidney affects the renal cortex, which appears brown, while the medulla remains uninvolved. Results showed only eleven cases diagnosed with the cloisonne kidney lesion among the examined sheep. This finding led to an estimated frequency rate of 0.059% for sheep cloisonne kidney in these regions.\n\nIn summary, sheep cloisonne kidney is a rare and incidental renal lesion marked by iron pigment-related basement membrane thickening in the renal cortex. The lesion is clinically silent and does not affect renal function. These metabolites inhibit the 11-\u03b2-hydrogenase type II enzyme (11\u03b2-HSD2), which normally converts cortisol to cortisone. These effects pose serious health risks, especially for individuals with preexisting cardiovascular conditions. Two recent meta-analyses comprising 18 and 26 studies respectively, have demonstrated statistically significant increases in both systolic (approximately 5.45 mmHg) and diastolic (around 3.19/1.74 mmHg) blood pressure associated with licorice intake.\n\nThis review highlights the dual nature of licorice candy and related licorice products: while licorice offers various health benefits, its metabolites\u2019 impact on cellular enzymes and blood pressure regulation underlines the importance of moderation. Due to its medicinal, industrial, and economic importance, interest in cultivating glasswort has increased in recent years. A key challenge in managing glasswort farms is determining the optimal harvest time, as glasswort seeds ripen rapidly and tend to fall with minimal disturbance. To address this, the appropriate harvest date can be identified by correlating the visible greenness and ripening stages of the glasswort plant with Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) values derived from remote sensing data.\n\nThis experimental study aimed to solve the harvest timing problem by relating changes in visually estimated color classes of the glasswort plant and its seedfall amount to NDVI values obtained from Sentinel-2 satellite imagery. The research involved analyzing data collected during the glasswort seedfall period, both in cultivated fields and natural habitats. A total of 41 Sentinel-2 images from 2018 to 2020 within the glasswort phenological period were evaluated. Some online products were likely adulterated or contained excessively high levels of active compounds. These pose safety concerns due to dose-dependent adverse effects (notably one sample with andrographolides) and potential pharmacokinetic interactions (notably one sample with piperine). As a consequence, the study advises consumers to avoid purchasing dietary supplements and combination products from unverified Internet sources and to rely on verified suppliers such as local pharmacies and health stores.\n\nThis work presents the first validated method tailored for the analysis of these complex combination products, which are increasingly prevalent in the market. also, hydrophobic residues contribute the most contact points, which agrees with the strong hydrophobic character of the mos2 nanomaterial. electrophysiology recordings using two-electrode voltage-clamp show that currents of kir3.2 and kv1.2 are both blocked by the mos2 nanoflakes in a concentration-dependent way. while the background k+ channel, k2p2 (trek-1), identified as a negative control, is not blocked by the mos2 nanoflakes. the large and rigid extracellular domain of k2p2 appears to protect the channel from disturbance by the nanoflakes. intrinsic chemical properties of mos2, together with the specific features of the channels, such as the electrostatic character and complex surface architecture, determine the critical details of the binding events. these findings might shed light on the potential nanotoxicology of mos2 nanomaterials and help us to understand the underlying molecular mechanism.",

Pediocin exhibits strong antimicrobial activity, particularly against Listeria monocytogenes, with high stability across a broad pH range (2\u201310) and temperatures up to 121 \u00b0C. Techniques such as fed-batch and immobilized-cell systems support industrial-scale production. Isolation and purification methods including chromatography, ultrafiltration, and aqueous two-phase systems are assessed for their suitability in processing pediocin for commercial use.\n\nFurther, pediocin's incorporation into bioactive packaging and nanocomposites is explored, increasing shelf life and safety of food products including wine. Its resistance to enzymes and heat facilitates its use in minimally processed foods, supporting hurdle technology and clean-label product development trends. "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03414402": "Fatty acid esters of ascorbic acid, also known as fatty acid ascorbyl esters, are liposoluble compounds with strong antioxidative properties. These esters can be synthesized through acylation of vitamin C using various acyl donors, catalyzed chemically or enzymatically. The enzymatic method, often preferred, offers regioselectivity, mild reaction conditions, and environmental benefits. Due to ascorbic acid\u2019s high polarity, common solvents with high Log P values are unsuitable; instead, polar organic solvents, ionic liquids, and supercritical fluids have been effectively employed as reaction media.\n\nSynthesis of fatty acid esters of ascorbic acid has involved fatty acids and their methyl-, ethyl-, vinyl esters, along with triglycerides. Utilizing activated acyl donors has improved molar conversion rates. Additionally, most studies have reported that an excess of acyl donor positively influences product yield. Strategies to shift the reaction equilibrium toward fatty acid esters of ascorbic acid focus on controlling water content. This includes adjusting initial water activity by pre-equilibrating the reaction mixture, exposing enzyme preparations to water vapor of saturated salt solutions, and removing generated water via molecular sieves or salt hydrate pairs.\n\nThe article aims to provide an overview of lipase-catalyzed procedures for the synthesis of fatty acid esters of ascorbic acid, highlighting their potential in food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical industries. However, commercialization faces challenges such as long reaction times, lack of efficient purification methods, and the high cost of lipases. Future directions include exploring new catalysts, developing continuous production processes, discovering more affordable acyl donors and reaction media, and establishing standard purification procedures that avoid large-scale use of non-biocompatible organic solvents. Addressing these challenges will facilitate broader application and industrial scalability of fatty acid esters of ascorbic acid.",

This study evaluated hornification by measuring drainage, fiber width, and water retention value of hardwood and softwood pulps at different stages: before and after sheet forming, and following various drying procedures reaching different solids content levels. These measurements revealed that as the water removal process progresses and solids content increases, both drainage and fiber width decrease, indicating that fibers become stiffer with increased water removal.\n\nWater retention value measurements further showed that hornification is a stepwise phenomenon closely linked to the water removal process. Significant reductions in fiber flexibility occur immediately during initial processing and again after a certain threshold of water removal is reached. The fibers must attain a specific solids content during the water removal process to exhibit hornification. Moreover, the presence of hydrogen bonds in water is crucial, as these bonds draw cellulose surfaces together, facilitating hornification. Experiments involving drying pulps from acetone, where hydrogen bonding is unavailable, highlighted the importance of these hydrogen bonds in the water removal process.\n\nThe mechanism driving hornification is believed to be dominated by hydrogen bonding and relates to the spacing between cellulose chains within the fiber wall. While hydrogen bonds are central, other types of bonds may also contribute, supporting the irreversibility of hornification observed during water removal. In summary, the water removal process is fundamental to cellulose hornification, affecting fiber rigidity and flexibility through alterations in hydrogen bonding and fiber structure. Understanding this process helps optimize drying and recycling methods for cellulosic materials.",

Historically, the malaria parasite was introduced into the Americas, including Hispaniola and the Caribbean, through the trans-Atlantic slave trade from the 16th to 19th centuries. More than 12 million Africans, many carrying the parasite due to its holoendemic presence in West Africa, were brought to the American continents. Despite expectations of a diverse, paraphyletic origin of American parasites reflecting multiple introductions, whole-genome sequencing and analyses of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) reveal that the American P. falciparum isolates form a well-supported monophyletic clade, distinct yet ancestrally related within a lineage alongside South American parasites.\n\nThis unexpected genetic uniformity in American parasites is best explained by a severe population bottleneck, attributed to the necessity for the parasite to adapt to new Anopheles mosquito vectors unique to the Caribbean and South America. The bottleneck led to the selection of rare African alleles in genes expressed during the mosquito stages of the parasite\u2019s lifecycle that are critical for transmission success. These alleles, containing multiple high-frequency or fixed nonsynonymous mutations, are prevalent in American parasite populations but rare in African isolates, underscoring adaptation to American vector species.\n\nThe findings emphasize how evolutionary pressures linked to American vectors shaped the current parasite population and provide novel genetic markers for mapping and monitoring P. falciparum movements in the Americas. Importantly, these data represent the first whole-genome sequences available from Haitian isolates, offering valuable insights for developing new transmission-blocking malaria vaccines targeting parasite proteins involved in successful vector transmission in the American context.
